So who is the first-term senator expected to announce a leadership ticket tilt with David Shoebridge ? Get your dirty hands off our kids, that is our message to the fossil fuel industry, who have no place in early-learning centres, in schools, or in our cultural institutions in this country. Children should go to school to get evidence-based education, not to be brainwashed by fossil fuel corporations seeking to build social licence… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Small fields, great diversity: How a diverse patchwork of crops helps birds
item.description: Birds are not only beautiful to look at and listen to; they also play important roles in nature. They eat pests and disperse seeds. They are generally considered indicators of a healthy environment. When birds thrive, soil and water quality often benefit as well. A new study published in the journal Landscape Ecology shows that growing a variety of crops in small field patches creates better habitats for birds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Engineered coating lets mitochondria retain their ability to produce energy
item.description: Researchers have coated mitochondria with innovative materials without compromising their function, according to a study by IRCCS Fondazione Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta (FINCB) and Politecnico di Milano. The research was conducted as part of the BraiNs joint laboratory, inaugurated in 2023. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NYC delivery workers injured at more than five times national rate under intense labor control by apps, survey finds
item.description: More than half of New York City's app-based food delivery workers have been injured on the job, and 40% meet the criteria for severe psychological distress, according to a new study from the CUNY Graduate School of Public Health and Health Policy (CUNY SPH), in partnership with the Worker's Justice Project (WJP). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Beyond temperature: How people experience urban heat
item.description: Urban heat is more than a matter of temperature. It can affect how people sleep, work, travel through the city and dress, and even how safe or comfortable they feel in public spaces. Yet these everyday consequences often remain invisible in conventional assessments of urban heat. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Alien life? Why the possibility of exoplanet LHS 1140b emitting helium gas is so exciting
item.description: This summer, exoplanet science—the study of planets orbiting stars beyond our sun—took a big step forward. Reports of helium gas escaping from the atmosphere of LHS 1140b propelled this exoplanet from the pages of scientific journals into the mainstream media. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons
item.description: Mindgard said it discovered in July that Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade developer's safety limits. Publicado también por: BBC News - Business. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: Nine generations of virtual dating reveal how fish shape their ideal mates
item.description: Fish have "designed" their perfect partners in a new experiment—revealing simple male preferences and more complex female tastes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Revisiting a Young Isaac Newton
item.description: Isaac Newton is typically portrayed as a solitary scientist with intense focus who was obsessed with power and deeply egotistical. But a new book by Caltech historians Jed Buchwald and Mordechai Feingold takes a deeper look at Newton's life in the two decades leading up to the 1687 publication of his groundbreaking text, Principia Mathematica, when he was 44. Using newly digitized scans of Newton's early writings, Buchwald and Feingold uncover a portrait of the young polymath as a curious and social scholar whose interests were often fleeting. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why monkeys handle conflicts better than we do
item.description: Conflicts with our colleagues, loved ones or team members can quickly stifle communication, heighten tensions and undermine relationships. However, a decision or compromise is not always enough to restore cooperation—for a solution to last, we must also repair the bond that will allow people to continue moving forward together. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rethinking liquid hydrogen storage with metal-organic frameworks
item.description: Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) is attractive for long-distance energy transport because of its high volumetric energy density. But even well-insulated tanks cannot completely prevent heat from entering. As the liquid warms, hydrogen evaporates and pressure builds, leading to boil-off losses during storage and transport. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How a new textile fabric could triple production in strawberry plants
item.description: A new textile used to cover strawberry plants more than tripled fruit yields in tunnel field tests without harming plant health. The technology could also significantly reduce water and pesticide use in strawberry fields. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wild tomatoes still hold the flavor we bred away: New map shows breeders where to look
item.description: Modern tomatoes are a breeding success story. Generations of selection have made them bigger, firmer, more productive and easier to ship. But that progress came at a cost. Domestication and breeding reduced much of the crop's genetic diversity, and flavor has proven stubbornly hard to breed back in. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Your car and its mobile app are probably handing over all kinds of data to tech companies
item.description: Researchers at Northeastern University found vehicles and their companion apps regularly shared detailed data with some of the largest tech companies. Fuente: TechCrunch.
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec

item.title: Light-driven nickel catalyst forms chemical bonds using less metal
item.description: Pharmaceuticals, fine chemicals, and agrochemicals are produced industrially using a wide range of chemical reactions. These processes need to become more efficient, less expensive, and more sustainable. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Christian amulets preserved Roman traditions of protection
item.description: For centuries, the Romans turned to amulets to protect themselves or their surroundings. Research by Ph.D. candidate Patricia Kret shows that this tradition continued into the early days of Christianity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New Irish language tool makes school more accessible for autistic children
item.description: A new Irish-language tool developed by researchers at Trinity College Dublin is allowing autistic children from Irish-language communities to participate more fully in school and their communities. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Molecular simulations reveal how an enzyme's shape guides molecular recognition
item.description: Enzymes are often described as molecular machines that recognize and process specific molecules. However, they are not rigid structures. Their shapes can change, affecting how molecules enter, interact with and remain within their active sites. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Opens 2027 Human Lander Challenge for Lunar Communications
item.description: NASA’s 2027 Human Lander Challenge is seeking ideas from college and university students to help address one of the most critical needs for sustained lunar exploration: reliable communications. As NASA prepares for long-term human presence on the Moon through the Artemis and Moon Base programs, communications systems will be just as important as spacecraft and […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Bailey G. Light

item.title: Dyed liquid crystals enable light-only control of optical components
item.description: A new technique for controlling optical components with light could help usher in a generation of high-efficiency signal-processing technology that could drive futuristic applications such as holographic video. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Physics-grounded AI framework aims to make predictions about new materials more testable
item.description: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to discover new materials, but conventional data-driven approaches can struggle to explain their predictions, work reliably beyond their training data and remain consistent with physical laws. A new perspective proposes a framework called Physics-Grounded Materials AI (PhysMat AI), which integrates fundamental physical knowledge into the materials discovery process. The research is published in the journal Advanced Functional Materials. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New index links changing ocean food webs to Bermuda's spiny lobster fishery
item.description: Spiny lobster larvae spend six to nine months drifting in the open ocean, feeding within the plankton community, before eventually settling into shallow-water habitats such as mangroves, seagrass beds or coral reefs. This means the number of young lobsters reaching Bermuda is strongly influenced by ocean conditions across the wider North Atlantic and Caribbean region. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: LISA to the rescue: Using light to fix cell division
item.description: Cell division is a complex process. At the heart of this complexity is a membraneless organelle called the centrosome, which is made up of more than 200 components. It is responsible for clustering mitotic spindles, threadlike structures needed to separate genetic material. It has long remained unclear which parts of the centrosome are necessary and sufficient for spindle assembly. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Genetic audit of wheat: Researchers determine the actual variability of a gene responsible for bread quality
item.description: A team at the University of Córdoba (UCO) has reviewed and updated the catalog of versions of the wheat gene GLU-B1, which is responsible for a protein that makes up gluten. The team has also made a collection of wheat representing the gene's true variability available to the research community. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Awards Orbital Safety Analysis Support Services Contract
item.description: NASA has awarded a contract to Omitron Inc. for the acquisition of orbital safety analysis services, which provide for critical protection of NASA spaceflight assets and astronaut lives. This indefinite-delivery contract is valued at approximately $23.5 million over a five-year period of performance and entails conjunction assessment screening services for all NASA uncrewed spacecraft, support […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: NASA Features Exploration, Science at International Space Conference
item.description: NASA will participate in the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, from Monday, Oct. 5, to Friday, Oct. 9, highlighting America’s leadership in human exploration to the Moon and Mars, advancing responsible exploration under the Artemis Accords, world-changing science, and support for the commercial space sector. The IAC, organized by the International Astronautical […] Fuente: NASA.

In early 2025, NASA joined scientists around the world in tracking asteroid 2024 YR4, which had a small chance of impacting Earth in 2032. As the international community studied it more closely, it was ultimately found to pose no threat to Earth — but the asteroid still provided a real-world test of the systems designed to protect our planets. We have the behind-the-scenes story. Tune in and watch Planetary Defenders: This Is Not an Exercise, our newest documentary, now streaming on NASA+. https://go.nasa.gov/46Jm361 | NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration

item.title: Protein signaling cascade helps explain how plants respond to touch
item.description: Plants cannot run away when the wind picks up, rain lashes down or a hungry herbivore begins chewing on their leaves. Instead, they must sense their surroundings and adapt. Now, researchers have uncovered an important piece of the puzzle of what happens inside plants when they are exposed to touch, injury or other physical stimuli. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New device measures curved mirrors' absolute shape to within 2 nanometers without touching them
item.description: Researchers at AIST have developed a device that measures the absolute surface profile of curved optical elements with high precision without touching them. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI structure prediction speeds discovery of 'molecular glues' to treat disease
item.description: A Baylor College of Medicine-led team has developed a strategy that combines the analysis of thousands of proteins with artificial intelligence to accelerate the discovery of small molecules called molecular glues to treat disease. Their approach, published in Nature Communications, has uncovered a new class of molecular glues that could neutralize harmful proteins linked to blood cancers and autoimmune diseases. The work also shows how AI-based structural modeling can help chemists optimize compounds well before experiments reveal how they work. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New feathered, winged dinosaur from China challenges our theories on bird and dinosaur evolution
item.description: A newly described feathered dinosaur found in northeastern China adds evidence supporting the theory that flight-related features evolved differently in various bird-like dinosaur groups. The findings, reported in Nature Communications, are based on an analysis of an exceptionally well-preserved fossil of a microraptorine (a small dinosaur with feathers and wings) found in a geological formation estimated to be between 145 and 100 million years old. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Under the Microscope: NASA-made material for moon manufacturing
item.description: Photos taken using a microscope reveal the colorful, kaleidoscope-like crystal structure of a new NASA-made material that could be used for manufacturing during future space missions. Developed at NASA's Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, the material could be created directly on the moon or Mars, allowing NASA to pack fewer supplies—saving weight and reducing launch costs. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Adds Blue Origin New Glenn 9×4 to Launch Services Contract
item.description: In accordance with a contract on-ramp clause, NASA has added Blue Origin’s New Glenn 9×4 launch service to the NASA Launch Services (NLS) II contract. The New Glenn 9×4 launch service will be available to NASA’s Launch Services Program Office to use for future missions. The NLS II contracts are multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts with an […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer M. Dooren

item.title: Inside the fossil fuel industry's push into Australian classrooms
item.description: At least 260 educational programs in Australia are sponsored by fossil fuel companies, according to a report by a climate advocacy group. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Morris

item.title: Mobile crisis response programs get new measures of their impact on police calls
item.description: Communities across the country are debating the role mobile crisis response programs can play in emergency response. These programs typically take calls from 911 dispatchers involving mental health, substance use, welfare checks and other situations that do not require a law enforcement response. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study finds trust is the missing ingredient for AI-driven food safety
item.description: Artificial intelligence promises to transform food safety by helping companies identify risks earlier, predict outbreaks and learn from patterns too rare for any one company to detect alone. But AI depends on one thing: large, diverse datasets. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: We can finally measure the damage each new coal, gas or oil project will do to people and nature
item.description: We have long known every tonne of carbon dioxide matters to the climate. But governments keep approving new fossil fuel projects—even as climate change worsens. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A new family of materials for efficiently converting sunlight into clean energy
item.description: Researchers at Oregon State University have developed a new family of materials that use light to produce hydrogen from water, opening the door to new ways of converting the sun's rays into clean energy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Arctic infrastructure was built on frozen ground—drones and digital twins can help spot the permafrost thaw coming
item.description: From the air, Wainwright, Alaska, looks like a perfectly stable band of homes and roads between the Chukchi Sea and a vast, flat tundra. But just below the surface, the frozen ground on which this town was built contains large bodies of ice. Along the eroding coastal bluffs, that hidden ice is becoming exposed and melting away. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mysterious giant carving may show a Kushite ruler and mark an ancient borderland
item.description: For centuries, a life-size petroglyph has stood over the rocky landscape of Miseeda in northern Sudan. Exactly who the figure carved into a granite hill represents remains uncertain, but researchers suspect it may depict an ancient Kushite ruler. In the 7th century CE, local builders constructed a Christian church directly around it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists call for protection and restoration of Africa's seagrass meadows
item.description: A team of African researchers has published the first comprehensive review of seagrass restoration activities across Africa's coastline. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Taylor Swift: My database of her 123,553 lyrics reveals hidden patterns
item.description: "It seems like all I ever do is change," Taylor Swift writes in the prolog to the bestselling album 1989 (Taylor's Version), released in 2023. In fact, change is a core part of the Swift marketing machine, which revolves around the evolution of her "eras." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Across six cultures, children step in when peers need help
item.description: A new study by an international research team provides the first systematic, cross-cultural comparison of how children help their peers. While previous research has mainly focused on how children help adults, often within the family, peer interactions play an equally important but far less studied role in children's social lives across many cultures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Pilots, aircrew face higher radiation-related cancer death rates, study finds
item.description: While the study of death records across 500 occupations is US based, experts say the finding could be similar in Australia and suggests more radiation monitoring of airline crew is needed. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Jacinta Bowler

item.title: 8-million-year-old rhino skull found in Crete
item.description: A rhinoceros skull at least 8 million years old has been found in the town of Sitia on Crete, the Greek news agency ANA reported Tuesday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Sets Crew-13 Launch, Docking Coverage
item.description: NASA will provide live coverage of prelaunch, launch, and docking activities for the agency’s SpaceX Crew‑13 mission to the International Space Station. Live coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online: https://www.nasa.gov/live Crew‑13 is scheduled to launch at 11:10 a.m. EDT, Thursday, Oct. 1, from Space Launch Complex 40 at […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Taveau

item.title: A series of videos from people inside the industry building AI technology echoed some of the ‘doomer’ warnings others have sounded recently.
item.description: A series of videos from people inside the industry building AI technology echoed some of the ‘doomer’ warnings others have sounded recently. THEVERGE.COM AI researchers put out videos saying superintelligence is ‘exactly as dangerous as it sounds’ Fuente: The Verge.

item.title: Chatbots as oracles: How AI is giving new life to the ancient practice of seeking answers from inscrutable sources
item.description: People are increasingly turning to AI for advice. A 2026 Pew report found that 10% of Americans use chatbots for emotional support or companionship. Some even find a charismatic leader in AI. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA has a Dragon dilemma, and there appear to be no good answers
item.description: So is SpaceX just being selfish or what? Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Eric Berger

item.title: Research shows poor mental health among politicians may impair decision-making
item.description: When political leaders disclose mental health challenges—as an increasing number of high-profile leaders have done in recent years—the public debate usually focuses on politicians' personal resilience or experiences. Yet behind these individual stories lies a far more consequential question for democracy: When elected representatives experience psychological distress, how does it alter the high-stakes choices they make on our behalf? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Suns set on hunt for giant planets in nearby binary system
item.description: New research led by the University of Michigan is helping set the stage for future observatories to characterize rocky planets outside our solar system, planets that could prove life isn't confined to Earth. The new research represents the most sensitive modern search for giant planets in a nearby binary system—a system with two stars orbiting each other—known as 70 Ophiuchi AB, or 70 Oph AB. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wolves did not save Yellowstone—why were we so desperate to believe they did?
item.description: You might be among the 46 million people who've seen a video showing how wolves changed Yellowstone, or you may have heard another version of the story. Yellowstone, which covers nearly 3,500 square miles (9,100 square kilometers) of the western United States, was the world's first national park. Its pioneering reintroduction of wolves, which began in 1995, set a worldwide precedent for conservation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Poner ventanas en las naves espaciales es clave para que los astronautas no se vuelvan locos. El problema es instalarlas
item.description: No valoramos la importancia de las ventanas, hasta que tenemos un baño sin ellas. O un piso de alquiler con ventanas a una tapia. O directamente un dormitorio sin ventanas. Pero si hay un lugar en el que las ventanas son más importantes todavía, este es el espacio . Sin embargo, durante mucho tiempo, no fueron una prioridad. En las misiones Mercury, las primeras estadounidenses en llevar humanos al espacio, los astronautas tuvieron que discutir con los ingenieros para lograr que incluyeran un ventanal en la cápsula. Desde entonces no ha hecho falta ninguna discusión, pero sí mucha… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: SpaceX's Starship rocket does its job during first orbital flight
item.description: SpaceX sent its Starship super-rocket on its first orbital flight—a shorter-than-planned test mission that put operational Starlink satellites into orbit for the first time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How ocean chemistry helped life keep breathing
item.description: Scientists have helped solve a longstanding mystery about how Earth remained habitable after oxygen first accumulated in its atmosphere more than 2 billion years ago, providing evidence that ancient ocean chemistry sustained life-friendly conditions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers find a fungus in Kentucky's forest grass that makes rare bug-fighting chemicals
item.description: Researchers at the University of Kentucky Martin-Gatton College of Agriculture, Food and Environment (CAFE) have discovered that a fungus living inside a common Kentucky woodland grass produces a rare combination of chemicals that likely helps protect the plant from hungry insects. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Un estudio ha identificado una clave para prevenir el Alzhéimer: algo tan sencillo como hacer ejercicio
item.description: El alzhéimer es una de esas enfermedades que de momento no podemos curar. Uno de los principales focos está puesto sobre todo en la prevención, puesto que queremos encontrar las mejores maneras de tener un cerebro lo más sano posible con el objetivo de ir reduciendo las 'papeletas' que tenemos para que esta enfermedad aparezca. Y el ejercicio parece que tiene un gran efecto protector aquí. Se ha estudiado. A finales del año pasado, en la revista Nature apareció un artículo donde se analizaban a 296 participantes cognitivamente sanos. A partir de esta muestra, se comenzó a medir su actividad… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: José A. Lizana

item.title: Extensive audit reveals gaps between Google AI answers and cited sources
item.description: Since its launch in 1998, Google, the world's leading search engine, has transformed how people find information online. For years, search results appeared as ranked lists of sources: Google decided what to show, but users decided what to read and whom to trust. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Plant lovers wanted: Study highlights demand for citizen science
item.description: Over the last several years, invasive plant and insect species have found their way into more and more social media feeds. From the tree of heaven to Bradford pear trees and the ubiquitous spotted lanternfly, home gardeners are spreading the word about problematic species to their networks. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA highlights lessons learned from Swift boost mission
item.description: A commercial mission to boost NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory ended without raising the spacecraft's orbit, but the agency and Katalyst Space gained experience that will benefit future in-space servicing programs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Survey reveals plastic 12,800 feet deep off Ecuador as beach waste rises
item.description: Plastic pollution is a growing threat to marine environments, with discarded waste reaching from coastlines to the deepest parts of the ocean. Now, a six-year study has revealed how quickly debris can accumulate on a beach in Ecuador, with one monitoring site collecting about 570 grams (1.25 pounds) of debris every week. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Losing our history and identity'—three B.C. glaciers on the brink of extinction
item.description: Three much-loved glaciers in British Columbia are set to disappear completely within a few decades, according to a Simon Fraser University study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Parasites that steer nocturnal hosts into water do not rely on lunar cycles, study finds
item.description: Like many parasites, nematomorphs are known to manipulate their hosts' behavior to complete their life cycles. Also known as horsehair worms, among other names, these creatures develop in their hosts' body cavities and lure their terrestrial arthropod victims into the water, where the parasites reproduce. Some species have even been observed to induce positive phototaxis, attracting the host toward horizontally polarized light reflected on the water's surface. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: The “constant sound of hammering and metal work” fills the air at this shipyard in Dhaka, Bangladesh, where massive ships are repaired and constructed... Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Studies map microclimates beneath solar panels to help native vegetation thrive in the shadow of renewable energy
item.description: Using solar energy is good for the environment, but look down, and the grass isn't always greener. Solar farms can generate massive amounts of renewable energy, but when they're built in natural areas, they change the growing conditions underneath the panels. That can make it easy for native grasses to be squeezed out by invasive weeds and non-native plants. On top of that, fast-growing turf or other non-native grasses are often used as a less costly, more convenient replacement in reclamation efforts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rotating light pattern reveals laser frequency in a single image
item.description: An international team of physicists has developed a new method for determining the precise color of laser light using an image that rotates as the laser's frequency shifts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Crew-13 Rocket and Spacecraft at Launch Pad
item.description: Ahead of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission launch, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft are vertical at the launch pad of Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida in this Sept. 27, 2026, photo. NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: Scandium's electrons may explain predicted room-temperature superconductivity
item.description: Scientists have confirmed the existence of a predicted room temperature superconductor, while explaining the microscopic mechanism that distinguishes it from a similar one discovered several years ago. The work, published in the journal Physical Review B, offers "a theoretical blueprint for the future design of superior superconductor hydrides" the physicists write. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tokyo suffers the longest streak of rainy days on record
item.description: Tokyo has recorded 34 consecutive days of rain, marking the longest such streak on record, according to Japan's weather agency. Publicado también por: Euronews. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Joshua Tree crossings planned in California’s Mojave Desert to protect wildlife with $6M-plus funding
item.description: Two wildlife crossings are planned over State Route 62 near Joshua Tree National Park in California’s Mojave Desert. The projects aim to reconnect fragmented habitats and reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions. Researchers are studying bighorn sheep, mountain lions and bobcats to guide the designs, with more than $6 million in grants supporting engineering, environmental studies and planning. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Identical hiring algorithms may create echo chambers that overlook stronger job candidates
item.description: AI tools are increasingly replacing human judgments in some settings. For instance, resume-screening algorithms are often used in hiring, where they may improve efficiency and consistency in decision-making. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study shows California's rodenticide restrictions are working, and flags new rodenticides rising in their place
item.description: New research from the Integral Ecology Research Center (IERC) offers some of the clearest evidence yet that California's efforts to restrict dangerous rodenticides are paying off in the wild, while also flagging a new contaminant that deserves close attention. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: India turns to corals and seagrass to shield against rising seas
item.description: Under a blazing sun, workers crouch on a shrinking island off India's southern coast, threading bright green seagrass shoots onto wooden frames before anchoring them to the ocean floor. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Opens Applications for Second Season of ORBIT Student Challenge
item.description: Following a successful inaugural year of ingenuity and career building, NASA ORBIT (Opportunities in Research, Business, Innovation, and Technology) has officially returned for a second season to bring university and college student innovation to the forefront of Earth technology development and deep-space exploration. Registration for the 2026–2027 challenge is open through Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Same plant species, different chemistry: Why chemotype labels matter
item.description: Plants of the same species can differ considerably in their chemical composition, affecting their smell, taste and even toxicity. A new study shows that the term "chemotype" has not been used consistently. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New statistical method can flag hidden anomalies in scientific datasets
item.description: A research team at the University of Vienna, led by pharmaceutical chemist Johannes Kirchmair, has developed a statistical method to identify hidden anomalies in scientific datasets. The method can be applied automatically to large datasets, making it easier for researchers to pinpoint those that need closer scrutiny. The approach improves the quality of data-driven research and supports the development of reliable AI applications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA ramps up support to get Boeing's astronaut capsule flying after Butch and Suni fiasco
item.description: NASA is throwing extra support and money behind Boeing's troubled astronaut capsule to get it fixed and flying again as soon as possible. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: An endangered frog nursery in LA cares for hundreds of tadpoles until they're ready for the wild
item.description: The transition from tadpole to juvenile frog is never easy—legs sprout, tails shrink and lungs develop for a life on land, all while being hunted by fish and other predators. Talk about growing pains. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Feeling like you are losing ground predicts suicidal ideation more than income or age
item.description: New research finds that people are far more likely to report suicidal ideation when they perceive their lives as getting worse relative to their recent past, rather than because of their income, age or health status alone. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient bird becomes second Australian species to be named from the Cretaceous period
item.description: A pair of exceptionally rare Cretaceous bird bones found at separate sites near Richmond, Queensland, reveal a previously unknown species—the second formally named Cretaceous bird from Australia. Cretaceous bird fossils are extremely scarce in Australia, with fewer than a dozen isolated bones reported, making these finds especially significant. The research is published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The molecular mechanism that regulates TMEM63B lipid scrambling
item.description: TMEM63B, a mechanosensitive lipid scramblase, has an autoinhibitory domain in its C-terminal tail that helps keep it inactive under resting conditions, researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo report. Changes to this regulatory region, particularly the Leu776 residue, reverse the inhibitory action and cause continuous lipid scrambling, disrupting normal phospholipid asymmetry. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Half a million older Scots facing fuel insecurity, study finds
item.description: Data from more than 4,000 adults across Scotland showed that fuel, food and financial insecurity are widespread, and more than 1 in 10 adults experience all three simultaneously. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Warming weakens Asian monsoon's reach into the Mediterranean
item.description: The South Asian summer monsoon has long been known to shape the Mediterranean climate thousands of kilometers away as part of a phenomenon known as the "monsoon–desert" mechanism. Through this mechanism, intense monsoon convection during the summer releases large amounts of heat into the atmosphere, triggering large-scale circulation changes that promote sinking air over the Mediterranean. This process suppresses clouds and rainfall and contributes to the Mediterranean region's hot, dry climate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Under the Microscope: NASA-Made Material for Moon Manufacturing
item.description: Photos taken using a microscope reveal the colorful, kaleidoscope-like crystal structure of a new NASA-made material that could be used for manufacturing during future space missions. Developed at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, the material could be created directly on the Moon or Mars, allowing NASA to pack fewer supplies — saving weight and […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Peeling crust beneath Italy's Apennines may explain why mountains stretch and squeeze
item.description: Extending some 1,200 kilometers (750 miles) along the length of Italy, the Apennine Mountains present a challenging puzzle for geologists. In some places, the mountains are steadily being stretched apart, while in regions just tens of kilometers away, they are squeezing together. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will open a window into the Milky Way
item.description: Look up at the night sky with the naked eye and it may seem like it rarely changes. Yet the universe is in constant flux. Stars drift through space, orbiting the center of the Milky Way as planets orbit them. They rotate, showing spots on their surfaces and sometimes producing violent outbursts that affect planetary atmospheres much like solar storms produce auroras on Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The novel on your nightstand may be doing more for your empathy and cognitive health than you think
item.description: A popular narrative across Instagram Reels, business podcasts and magazine covers is that people who are smart and serious about growth read nonfiction. Nonfiction directly provides factual information and real-world knowledge, whereas fiction, like novels and poetry, is treated as a less practical cousin. Now, a recent study has asked whether fiction really is just entertainment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Diving into an out-of-sync galaxy
item.description: Galaxies are like snowflakes: No two are exactly alike, even the spirals. The Hubble Space Telescope took a close look at the distant spiral NGC 4693 and found intriguing hints about its past. For one thing, this member of the Virgo Cluster seems to have a central region that's rotating out of sync with its spiral arms and bulge. Those arms don't seem to connect to the central region, and the bulge itself seems to extend above the plane of the galaxy. In other words, there seems to be a decoupling between the arms and the bulge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Biologists may have discovered two of the world's loudest birds
item.description: University of Massachusetts Amherst's Jeff Podos and his former graduate student João C.T. Menezes have identified two contenders for the title of world's loudest bird: the bare-throated bellbird and the red-legged seriema. Their findings also help explain why some birds are so much louder than others. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nature-strip gardens boost biodiversity, bugs and social benefits
item.description: University of Melbourne researchers have found that planting native gardens on suburban nature strips can boost urban biodiversity, with insect numbers increasing sevenfold and the number of species approximately doubling. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Perceived motives help explain why some online campaigns fail to mobilize support
item.description: Flinders University researchers have examined the role social media plays in expanding social movements and found that perceptions of online activists' motives can significantly affect others' willingness to participate. The study is published in the journal New Media & Society. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wearable nanotech could combat nerve agents
item.description: Nanoparticles could someday provide a new way to help soldiers fight back against deadly nerve agents on the front lines. In a new study, Northwestern University scientists developed a nanoparticle-based compound that, when mixed into clothing dyes, could limit the impact of chemicals commonly found in pesticides, insecticides and nerve agents. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sneakers to Scrubs mentorship program shows data-backed promise
item.description: A new study highlights the promising early impact of Sneakers to Scrubs (S2S), a medical pathways program founded by Black medical students and former athletes to address the severe underrepresentation of Black men in medicine. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Overlooked lakes may be helping to keep the Northern Hemisphere cool
item.description: Lakes may cover only a small fraction of Earth's surface, but new research suggests they play a bigger role in regulating the planet's climate than previously recognized. By reflecting sunlight back into space when covered in snow and ice, lakes in the Northern Hemisphere have a stronger cooling effect than the surrounding land. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New sound catalog reveals who's who in the world of killer whales
item.description: A new open-access catalog of whale calls will help researchers and orca enthusiasts identify distinct killer whale populations, clans and family groups by their vocalizations alone. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: En 1971, un astronauta llevó 500 semillas hasta la Luna. Medio siglo después son árboles gigantes repartidos por la Tierra
item.description: En 1971, cuando la NASA preparaba el Apollo 14 , alguien decidió aprovechar el viaje para enviar hasta la Luna un cargamento bastante más extraño que cualquier instrumento científico: cientos de semillas de árboles. Viajaron hasta allí, dieron 34 vueltas alrededor de nuestro satélite y regresaron a la Tierra después de sobrevivir incluso a un accidente que hizo pensar que habían quedado destruidas. Más de medio siglo después, aquella diminuta carga se ha convertido en algo enorme. Semillas rumbo a la Luna. La idea nació de una colaboración entre la NASA y el Servicio Forestal de Estados… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: The ice blasting from Saturn's moon Enceladus is stranger than scientists realized
item.description: Enceladus may naturally separate and concentrate chemicals from its hidden ocean as droplets slowly freeze and shatter on their way into space. The process could explain Cassini’s puzzling ice-grain chemistry while giving future spacecraft a powerful advantage in searching for organic compounds and clues to life. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Investigadores crean aeronaves ultraligeras para explorar una región casi desconocida de la Tierra. Su truco: surfear la luz del Sol
item.description: Entre la estratosfera y la termosfera se encuentra una franja en la que termina el alcance de los aviones y globos, pero también donde empieza el dominio de los satélites. Se trata de la mesosfera y, en su parte más alta a unos 70 km, hay una zona inexplorada que se ha apodado con humor científico como ignorosfera. Es extremadamente difícil de estudiar y el motivo es un problema físico. A esa altitud hay tan poco aire que un avión convencional o un globo no pueden mantenerse a flote, pero el aire restante es suficiente para frenar cualquier satélite y hacerlo caer. item.description: China is offering the world’s brightest young scientists generous 15-year research grants for free exploration, as the country accelerates its drive to become a global science powerhouse. Dou Xiankang, director of the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), the country’s top funder of basic research, told a recent academic forum that the agency was selecting a group of the brightest researchers under 35 for long-term financial backing. item.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
item.description: Image: This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us. MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the… Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Getting AI 'drunk' makes it more likely to break rules, research finds
item.description: A study finds AI models are more likely to answer harmful questions or mishandle confidential information when told to act drunk. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

Esto es necesario por muchos motivos , ya que es útil para alargar la vida de los satélites, pero también sirve para emprender viajes espaciales mucho más largos, tanto en tiempo como en distancia. item.title: AI identifies Senegal's smallholder crops 84% of the time using limited training data
item.description: Food in Senegal is mostly grown on small-scale, rain-dependent farms, leaving much of the population vulnerable to climate shocks, according to the World Food Programme. However, satellite crop-mapping technologies designed to monitor the impact of climate on farming are largely beyond the reach of the West African country. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 55-million-year-old fossil bird shows how trogons evolved their unusual feet
item.description: A fossil of Daniatrogon kochi, discovered in Denmark, provides insights into the evolution of trogon feet. Researchers found that the trogons' unique foot morphology developed gradually over time. The fossil also shows changes in the shape of their beaks, which were narrower than those of modern species. Additionally, early trogoniforms displayed more varied beak and foot shapes, indicating a diverse ecology. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
